verses.1: Forward have flowed the streams of power, of this the mighty one effused, Of him who waits upon the Gods.
verses.2: The singers praise him with their song, and learned priests adorn the steed Born as thelight that merits laud.
verses.3: These things thou winnest quickly, while men cleanse thee, Soma, nobly rich!
verses.4: This Brahman, comer at the due time, named Indra, is renowned and praised.
verses.5: To thee alone, O Lord of Strength, go, as it were, all songs of praise.
verses.6: Like streams of water on their way, let bounties, Indra, flow from thee!
verses.7: Even as a car to give us aid, we draw thee nigh to favour us, Strong in thy deeds, quelling attack, Indra, Lord, mightiest! of the brave.
verses.8: Great in thou power and wisdom, strong, with thought that comprehendeth all! Wide hast thou spread in majesty.
verses.9: Thou very mighty one, whose hands by virtue of thy greatness wield The golden bolt that beaks its way!
verses.10: He who hath lighted up the joyous castle, wise courser like the steed of cloudy heaven, Bright like the Sun with hundredfold existence
verses.11: He, doubly born, hath spread in his effulgence through the three luminous realms, through all the regions, Best sacrificing Priest where waters gather.
verses.12: Priest doubly born, he through his love of glory hath in his keeping all things worth the choosing. The man who brings him gifts hath noble offspring.
verses.13: Agni, with hymns may we now accomplish that which thou lovest, Strength, like a horse auspicious, with service!
verses.14: For, Agni, thou art now the promoter of strength auspicious, Lofty sacrifice, power effective.
verses.15: Through these our praises, come thou to meet us, bright as the sunlight, Agni, kindly with all thy faces!
verses.16: Immortal Jatavedas, thou bright-hued refulgent gift of Dawn. Agni, this day to him who pays oblations bring the Gods who waken with the morn!
verses.17: For thou art offering-bearer, well-loved messenger, and charioteer of holy rites. Accordant with the Asvins and with Dawn grant us heroic strength and lofty fame!
verses.18: The old hath waked the young Moon from his slumber who runs his circling course with many round him Behold the God's high wisdom in its greatness: he who died yesterday to-day is living.
verses.19: Strong is the red Bird in his strength, great hero, who from of old bath had no nest to dwell in. That which he knows is truth and never idle: he wins and gives the wealth desired of many.
verses.20: Through these Thunderer gained strong manly vigour, through whom he waxed in stren gth to slaughter Vritra; These who through might of actual operation sprang forth as Gods in course of Law and Order.
verses.21: Here is the Soma ready pressed: of this the Maruts, yea, of this Self-luminous, the Asvins, drink.
verses.22: Of this, moreover, purified, set in three places, procreant, Drink Varuna, Mitra, Aryaman.
verses.23: Yea, Indra, like the Hotar-priest, will in the early morning drink, At pleasure, of the milky juice:
verses.24: Verily, Surya, thou art great; truly, Aditya, thou art great. O most admired for greatness of thy majesty, God, by thy greatn.ess thou art great.
verses.25: Yea, Surya, thou art great in fame: thou evermore, O God, art great. Thou by thy greatness art the Gods' High-Priest, divine, farspread unconquerable light.
verses.26: Come, Lord of rapturous joys, to our libations with thy bay steeds, come With bay steeds to our flowing juice!
verses.27: Known as best Vritra-slayer erst, as Indra $atakratu, come With bay steeds to our flowing juice!
verses.28: For, Vritra-slayer, thou art he who drinks these drops of Soma come With bay steeds to our flowing juice!
verses.29: Bring to the wise, the great, who waxeth mighty your offerings and make ready your devotion. Go forth to many tribes as man's controller!
verses.30: For Indra the sublime, the far-pervading, have singers generateo prayer and praises; The sages never violate his statutes.
verses.31: The choirs have established Indra King for ever for victory him, whose anger is resistless: And for the bays' Lord strengthened those he loveth.
verses.32: If I, O Indra, were the lord of riches ample as thine own, I would support the singer, God who scatterest wealth! and, not abandon him to woe.
verses.33: Each day would I enrich the man who sang my praise, in whatsoever place he were. No kinship is there better, Maghavan, than thine: a father even, is no more.
verses.34: Here thou the call of the juice-drinking press-stone: mark thou the sage's hymn who sings and lauds thee! Take to thine inmost self these adorations!
verses.35: I know and ne'er forget the hymns and praises of thee, theconqueror, of thy power immortal. Thy name I ever utter, self-refulgent!
verses.36: Among mankind many are thy libations, and many a time the pious sage invokes thee. O Maghavan, be not long distant from us!
verses.37: Sing strength to Indra that shall. set his chariot in the foremost place! Giver of room in closest fight, slayer of foes in shock of war, be thou our great encorager! Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of our weak mies!
verses.38: Thou didst destroy the Dragon: thou sentest the rivers down to Earth. Foeless, O Indra, wast thou born. Thou tendest well each choicest thing. Therefore we draw us close to thee. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of our weak enemies! Destroyed be all malignitics and all our enemy's designs!
verses.39: Thy bolt thou castest at the foe, O Indra, who would smite us dead: thy liberal bounty gives us wealth. Let the weak bowstrings break upon the bows of our weak enemies!
verses.40: Rich be the praiser of one rich and liberal, Lord of days! like thee: High rank be his who lauds the juice!
verses.41: His wealth who hath no store of kine hath ne'er found out recited laud, Nor song of praises that is sung.
verses.42: Give us not, Indra, as a prey unto the scornful or the proud: Help, mighty one, with power and might!
verses.43: Come hither, Indra, with thy bays, come thou to Kanva's eulogy! Ye by command of yonder Dyaus, God bright by day! have gone to heaven.
verses.44: The stones' rim shakes the Soma here like a wolf worrying a sheep. Ye by command of yonder Dyaus, God bright by day I have gone to heaven.
verses.45: May the stone bring thee as it speaks, the Soma-stone with ringing voice! Ye by command of yonder Dyaus, God bright by day! have gone to heaven.
verses.46: For Indra flow most rich in sweets, O Soma, bringing him delight!
verses.47: Bright, meditating sacred song, these juices have sent Vayu forth.
verses.48: They were sent forth to feast the Gods, like chariots speeding in the race.
verses.49: Agni I deem our Hotar priest, munificent wealth-giver, Son of Strength, who knoweth all that is even as the Sage who knoweth all. Lord of fair rites, a God with form erected turning to the Gods, he when the flame hath sprung forth from the holy oil, the offered fatness, longs for it as it grows bright.
verses.50: We, sacrificing, call on the best worshipper thee eldest of Angirasas, singer! with hyrnns, thee, brilliant one! with singers' hymn; Thee, wandering round, as 'twere the sky, thee who art Hotar-priest of men, whom, Bull with hair of flame, the people must observe, tile people that he speed them on.
verses.51: He with his blazing Power refulgent far and wide, he verily it iswho conquers demon foes, conquers the demons like an axe: At whose close touch things solid partg and what is stable yields he keeps his ground and flinches not,like trees. Subduing all from the skilled archer flinches not.
verses.52: O Agni, strength and fame are thine: thy fires blaze forth on high, O thou refulgent God! Sage, passing bright, thou givest to the worshipper with power, the wealth that merits laud.
verses.53: With brilliantg purifying sheen, with perfect sheen thou liftest up thyself in light. Thou, visiting both thy mothers, aidest them as son; thou joinest close the earth and heaven.
verses.54: O Jatavedas, Son of Strength, rejoice thyself, gracious, in our fair hymns and songs! In thee have they heaped viands various, many formed; wealthborn, of wondrous help are they.
verses.55: Agni, spread forth, as ruler, over living things: give wealth, to us, immortal God! Thou shinest out from beauty fair to look upon: thou leadest us to beauteous Power.
verses.56: I laud the Sage, who orders sacrifice, who hath great riches under his control. Thou givest blest award of good, and plenteous food, thou givest wealth that wins success.
verses.57: The men have set before them, for his favour, Agni, strong, visible to all, the holy. Thee, Lord divine, with ears to hear, most famous, mens' generations magnify with praise-songs.
verses.58: Agni, he conquers by thine aid that brings him store of valiant sons and does great deeds, Whose bond of friendship is thy choice.
verses.59: Thy spark is black and crackling; kindled in due time, O bounteous, it is taken up. Thou art the dear friend of the mighty Mornings: thou shinest in glimmerings of the night.
verses.60: Him, duly coming, as their germ have plants received: this Agni have maternal Waters brought to life. So, in like manner, do the forest trees and plants bear him within them and produce him evermore.
verses.61: Agni grows bright for Indra: he shines far resplendent in the sky: He sends forth offspring like a queen.
verses.62: The sacred hymns love him who wakes and watches: to him who watches the holy verses. This Soma saith to him Who wake my dwelling in thy friendship.
verses.63: Agni is watchful, and the Richas love him: Agni is watchful, Sama hymns approach him. Agni is watchful, to him saith this Soma, I rest and have my dwelling in thy friendship.
verses.64: Praise to the friends who sit in front! to those seated together,praise I use the hundred-footed speech speech.
verses.65: I use the hundred-footed speech, I sing what hath a thousand paths, Gayatra, Trishtup, Jagat hymn.
verses.66: Gayatra, Trishtup, Jagat hymn,the forms united and complete, Have the Gods made familiar friends.
verses.67: Agni, is light, light is Agni, Indra is light, light is Indra Surya is light, light is Surya.
verses.68: O Agni, turn again with strength, turn thou again with food and life: Save us again from grief and woe!
verses.69: O Agni, turn again with wealth sprinkle thou us from everyside. With thine own all-supporting stream!
verses.70: If I, O Indra, were like thee, the single ruler over wealth. My worshipper should be rich in kine.
verses.71: I should be fain, O Lord of power, to strengthen and enrich thesage, Where I the ford of herds of kine.
verses.72: Thy goodness, Indra, is a cow yielding in plenty kine and steeds. To worshippers who press the juice.
verses.73: Yea, Waters, ye bring health and bliss: so help ye us to energy. That we may look on great delight!
verses.74: Give us a portion of the dew, the most auspicious that ye have, Like mothers in their longing love!
verses.75: For you we gladly go to hirn to whose abode ye speed us on, And, Waters, give us procreant strength!
verses.76: May Vata breathe his balm on us, healthful, delightful to our heart: May he prolong our days of life!
verses.77: Thou art our father, Vata, yea, thou art our brother and our friend: So give us strength that we may live!
verses.78: The store of Amrit that laid away yonder, O Vata, in thine home-- Give us strength that we may live!
verses.79: The fleet steed wearing divers forms, the eagle bearing his golden raiment to his birthplace, Clothed in due season with the light of Surya, red, hath begot the sacrifice in person.
verses.80: Multiform seed he laid in waters, lustre which gathered on the earth and there developed. In the mid-air establishing his greatness, he cries aloud, seed of the vigorous courser.
verses.81: He hath, enduing thousand robes that suit him, as sacrifice upheld the light of Surya, Giver of ample gifts in hundreds, thousands, supporter of the heavens, earth's Lord and ruler.
verses.82: They gaze on thee with longing in their spirit, as on a strong-winged bird that mounteth sky-ward; On thee with wings of gold, Varuna's envoy, the Bird that hasteneth to the home of Yama.
verses.83: Erect, to heaven hath the Gandharva mounted, pointing at us his many-coloured weapons: Clad in sweet raiment beautiful to look on, for he, as light, produceth forms that please us..
verses.84: When as a spark he cometh ilear the ocean, looking with vulture's eye as Law commandeth, His lustre, joying in its own bright splendour, maketh dear glories in the loftiest region.
